Cysteine protease with an established human-drug-discovery chemotype AND an existing tick-genus-specific inhibition assay with real nanomolar IC50 data. Catalytic residues, fold, and validated small-molecule binders are all known from a very close congener (Ixodes ricinus). Given this is also flagged as having no detectable pollinator homolog, this looks like the single strongest lead in chunk 6.

B7PJS6.family: TRAFAC-class translation-factor GTPase superfamily, classic translation factor GTPase family, LepA/EF4 subfamily (mitochondrial GUF1 ortholog)
B7PJS6.family_evidence: UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the TRAFAC class translation factor GTPase superfamily... LepA subfamily'; InterPro IPR006297 (EF-4 family); Pfam PF00009 (GTP_EFTU), PF00679 (EFG_C), PF14492 (EFG_III), PF06421 (LepA_C); UniProt name 'Translation factor GUF1 homolog, mitochondrial'
B7PJS6.verification_note: RIBOSOMAL ANNOTATION CHECKED AND CORRECTED: B7PJS6 is NOT a structural ribosomal protein. It is GUF1, the mitochondrial ortholog of bacterial LepA/EF4 -- a translational GTPase (fidelity/proofreading factor) that transiently, GTP-dependently binds the ribosome to catalyze a one-codon backward tRNA translocation on improperly translocated ribosomes. It is a free-standing enzyme (GTP hydrolase, EC 3.6.5.-) that acts ON the ribosome, not a component OF the ribosome. Separately, the project's own local final_targets.json record has function_class='Enzyme - Protease' for this target, which is also incorrect (it is a GTPase, not a protease) -- likely a keyword-matching artifact from the annotation pipeline. Recommend correcting function_class to something like 'Enzyme - GTPase / translation factor' and NOT excluding it as 'ribosomal' since it is a genuine enzyme with a defined nucleotide pocket, unlike a true structural ribosomal protein (compare B7PY76 below, which IS a ribosome-biogenesis scaffold protein and a much weaker target).
B7PJS6.oligomeric_evidence: E. coli LepA/EF4 solved bound to the Thermus thermophilus 70S ribosome (PDB 5J8B with GDPCP; PDB 4W2E with GDP + P-site tRNA) -- in both, LepA/EF4 is a single monomeric 5-domain protein transiently docked at the ribosomal A-site region. It is not part of a fixed ribosomal-protein oligomer and has not been crystallized as a self-oligomer; same monomeric architecture as other translational GTPases (EF-Tu, EF-G).
B7PJS6.binding_site_location: GTPase active site (G-domain: P-loop/Walker A, switch I/II, conserved catalytic His81 in T. thermophilus numbering) is INTRA-subunit, within the N-terminal G-domain of the single polypeptide -- the same class of site targeted by antibiotics against other bacterial translational GTPases (EF-G, EF-Tu, IF2). The protein's larger functional role (remodeling A-site tRNA) is an inter-molecular protein-RNA interaction with the ribosome, but the nucleotide pocket relevant to small-molecule docking is intra-subunit.
B7PJS6.site_residues_known: Yes at the family level: conserved catalytic His81 (T. thermophilus EF4 numbering) required for ribosome-stimulated GTP hydrolysis, structurally equivalent to the catalytic histidine in EF-G/EF-Tu; canonical Walker A/B and G1-G5 GTPase-box motifs are conserved. Exact tick/mitochondrial-numbering residues not confirmed in this pass.
B7PJS6.characterized_relatives: E. coli EF4/LepA bound to T. thermophilus 70S ribosome with GDPCP (PDB 5J8B) and with GDP+P-site tRNA (PDB 4W2E) -- both are ribosome complexes with a non-hydrolyzable nucleotide analog, not a drug-like small-molecule ligand. No apo or drug-bound crystal structure of an isolated LepA/GUF1 G-domain was found. Human/yeast GUF1 itself is not structurally characterized (yeast guf1-knockout reported to have no clear phenotype).
B7PJS6.chembl_target: None found. No ChEMBL target entry for LepA/EF4/GUF1 was located; translational-GTPase drug discovery precedent exists for EF-G/EF-Tu/IF2 but not specifically this subfamily.
B7PJS6.druggability_note: Mechanistically druggable in principle (canonical nucleotide-binding GTPase pocket, same structural class as validated antibiotic targets), but no known inhibitor chemotype exists for LepA/EF4/GUF1 specifically. IMPORTANT CAUTION: this is a MITOCHONDRIAL translation factor, broadly conserved from bacteria through human mitochondria -- an off-target hit against host (dog/human) mitochondrial GUF1 is a real possibility and would need dedicated G-domain-level BLAST/selectivity review, not just the whole-protein identity score already on file.

Q8T9S4.family_evidence: UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the tetraspanin (TM4SF) family'; Pfam PF00335; InterPro IPR000301, IPR018499, IPR008952
Q8T9S4.oligomeric_state: COMPLEX (functions via lateral clustering into tetraspanin-enriched microdomains with partner proteins); core fold is a 4-TM-helix monomer
Q8T9S4.oligomeric_evidence: Human full-length CD81 crystal structure (PDB 5TCX) is a single 4-TM-helix monomer with an intramembrane cholesterol pocket formed by the convergence of its own four helices. The extracellular EC2 domain of CD81 (PDB 1G8Q apo, 6U9S + Fab) crystallizes as an antiparallel homodimer in some forms, but functionally tetraspanins are understood to act as monomers that laterally cluster into tetraspanin-enriched microdomains (TEMs) with various partner membrane proteins, not as a fixed-stoichiometry hetero-oligomer.
Q8T9S4.binding_site_location: Two candidate sites: (1) an INTRA-subunit intramembrane cholesterol-binding cavity formed by convergence of the four transmembrane helices near the inner leaflet (validated ligand: cholesterol, CD81 PDB 5TCX); (2) the extracellular EC2 domain surface, which mediates protein-protein/antibody/viral-receptor interactions and is where the EC2-EC2 dimer interface sits -- this would be INTER-subunit if targeting the observed EC2 dimer interface. Most defined small-molecule-relevant pockets described in the literature are the intra-subunit cholesterol cavity.
Q8T9S4.site_residues_known: Not documented for this tick ortholog specifically; human CD81 cholesterol-pocket residues are structurally defined (Zimmerman et al. 2016) but sequence is divergent -- no motif transferable with confidence to Q8T9S4.
Q8T9S4.characterized_relatives: Human CD81 full-length, LIGAND-BOUND with cholesterol -- PDB 5TCX. CD81 EC2 domain -- PDB 1G8Q (apo), 6U9S (+ Fab). Related tetraspanin EC2 domains solved for CD9, CD53, Tspan15 (PDB 6K4J, 6WVG, 7RDB per search results, not independently re-verified).
Q8T9S4.chembl_target: None found as a direct small-molecule inhibition target in this pass; tetraspanins are chiefly pursued via antibodies/PPI biologics (e.g. anti-CD81 for HCV entry blockade), not curated ChEMBL enzyme-style targets.
Q8T9S4.druggability_note: Non-enzymatic 4-TM scaffold protein, no catalytic site. The cholesterol-binding intramembrane pocket (CD81 precedent) is the only defined druggable cavity in the family. Likely LOWER priority than the enzymes in this batch for classical active-site docking; a lipid-mimetic or fragment-based approach targeting the intramembrane pocket would be the more realistic route if pursued.

B7QJZ7.family: ATP synthase F1 complex, gamma subunit family
B7QJZ7.family_evidence: Local final_targets.json InterPro cross-references (recovered pre-deletion): IPR000131 (ATP synthase F1 complex gamma subunit family), IPR023632 (conserved site), IPR035968 (superfamily)
B7QJZ7.note_deleted_accession: Deleted from UniProt 2026-01; config.py TARGET_PROVENANCE anchor = EMBL_CON:EEC19169 (tier 3, UPI00018EC04A).
B7QJZ7.oligomeric_evidence: F1Fo-ATP synthase central stalk = gamma+delta+epsilon subunits, embedded within a >20-subunit, multi-megadalton rotary-motor membrane complex (well established across all kingdoms; solved structures of the full complex and isolated F1 catalytic head include an E. coli F1-ATPase autoinhibited-conformation structure). Gamma is a single asymmetric coiled-coil subunit that physically inserts into and rotates within the surrounding alpha3-beta3 catalytic hexamer -- an inherently INTER-subunit relationship, since gamma's entire function is defined by its interface with that ring.
B7QJZ7.binding_site_location: No independent catalytic site exists on gamma itself -- ATP hydrolysis/synthesis chemistry occurs at the alpha/beta subunit interfaces of the F1 head, NOT on gamma. Gamma's role is purely mechanical/rotational (central shaft) plus regulatory (its C-terminal domain can wrap around the alpha3beta3 ring in an auto-inhibited state and block rotation). Any pocket identified by fpocket on an isolated monomeric gamma model is very unlikely to be the physiologically relevant site -- this is precisely a case of the inter-subunit binding-site problem this whole research task was commissioned to catch: gamma normally functions embedded within the alpha3beta3 ring, and the biologically relevant surface is the ring, not gamma's own exposed face.
B7QJZ7.site_residues_known: Not applicable to gamma itself for catalysis. The auto-inhibitory C-terminal-domain interaction with the alpha3beta3 ring is structurally documented in bacterial ATP synthase but is a distinct regulatory mechanism, not a conventional small-molecule active site on gamma.
B7QJZ7.characterized_relatives: E. coli F1-ATPase, autoinhibited conformation (Nat Struct Mol Biol 10.1038/nsmb.2058). Mycobacterium tuberculosis ATP synthase is an actively pursued TB drug target, but the validated druggable subunit there is Fo (c-ring; bedaquiline's target), not F1-gamma -- relevant as proof that ATP synthase CAN be drugged, but pointing away from gamma specifically.
B7QJZ7.chembl_target: CHEMBL4295752 (ATP synthase F1 complex subunit gamma, mitochondrial, Homo sapiens) exists as a ChEMBL target entry, but this likely reflects target bookkeeping rather than a validated inhibitor chemotype specifically against gamma -- known ATP-synthase drugs (bedaquiline, oligomycin) act on Fo/the c-ring, not F1-gamma.
B7QJZ7.druggability_note: STRUCTURAL RED FLAG for this project's monomer-based docking approach: gamma's biological binding surface is defined entirely by its interface with the alpha3beta3 catalytic ring -- an inter-subunit relationship by definition, exactly the failure mode described in this task's motivation. An fpocket-predicted pocket on an isolated monomeric gamma model is very unlikely to correspond to a real, exploitable site. The field's actual validated ATP-synthase drug target is the membrane-embedded Fo c-ring (bedaquiline precedent), a completely different subunit not represented by this accession. Recommend LOW priority for monomer-based docking; would need explicit alpha3beta3gamma complex modeling if pursued further.

B7SP57.family_evidence: UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the GST superfamily'; CDD explicitly hits GST_C_Delta_Epsilon (cd03177) and GST_N_Delta_Epsilon (cd03045) subfamily models -- specific class assignment, not just superfamily; Pfam PF00043 (GST_C) + PF02798 (GST_N); InterPro IPR004045, IPR004046, IPR040079
B7SP57.oligomeric_evidence: UniProt SUBUNIT annotation for this exact target (B7SP57) explicitly states 'Homodimer' -- direct evidence. Consistent with the entire cytosolic GST superfamily (all classes function as obligate homo- or hetero-dimers) and specifically with solved insect Delta/Epsilon GST structures: Anopheles gambiae delta-class agGSTd1-6 (PDB 1PN9, dimer, LIGAND-BOUND with S-hexyl glutathione inhibitor), A. gambiae epsilon-class (PDB 2IMI/2IMK/2IL3, dimers), Musca domestica delta-class MdGSTD1 (dimer, LIGAND-BOUND with glutathione), Drosophila epsilon-class DmGSTE6 (PDB 4YH2, dimer).
B7SP57.binding_site_location: Each subunit contributes its own G-site (glutathione-binding, thioredoxin-fold N-domain, mostly intra-subunit) and H-site (hydrophobic co-substrate pocket, C-domain, intra-subunit). SPECIFIC EXCEPTION worth flagging: the Epsilon class has a documented 'class-conserved subunit interface motif' (the 'Epsilon clasp motif') that directly contacts and helps position glutathione in the active site FROM THE OTHER SUBUNIT -- i.e. for epsilon-class GSTs the active site has a genuine inter-subunit contribution, unlike the more purely intra-subunit active sites of most other GST classes. If this target is epsilon-class specifically (vs delta), this nuance matters for pocket definition.
B7SP57.site_residues_known: Yes at the family level: Delta/Epsilon classes use a catalytic active-site Tyr (not Ser/Cys as in other GST classes) that stabilizes the glutathione thiolate. S-hexyl-glutathione-bound agGSTd1-6 (PDB 1PN9, 2.0 A) and glutathione-bound MdGSTD1 (1.4 A) directly define the G-site residues for this class.
B7SP57.characterized_relatives: Anopheles gambiae delta-class agGSTd1-6 -- PDB 1PN9, LIGAND-BOUND (S-hexyl glutathione inhibitor), 2.0 A, DDT-resistance-associated. A. gambiae epsilon-class agGSTe2/agGSTe (highest DDT-detoxifying activity in the genus, ~350x delta-class) -- PDB 2IMI, 2IMK, 2IL3. Musca domestica delta-class MdGSTD1 -- LIGAND-BOUND with glutathione, 1.4 A. Drosophila melanogaster epsilon-class DmGSTE6 -- PDB 4YH2. An extremely well-characterized, directly relevant (arthropod, same enzyme class implicated in insecticide/acaricide resistance) family with multiple high-resolution ligand-bound structures.
B7SP57.chembl_target: General mammalian GST ChEMBL entries exist (CHEMBL3409 GST A1 human, CHEMBL2423/CHEMBL2141 GST theta-1, etc.) but these are the WRONG class (Alpha/Theta, mammalian) -- no insect Delta/Epsilon-class ChEMBL single-protein target was found in this search pass. The relevant chemical matter for this class lives in the primary DDT/insecticide-resistance literature rather than ChEMBL's curated bioactivity set. Mark as UNKNOWN/not found for the correct (insect Delta/Epsilon) class specifically.
B7SP57.druggability_note: One of the two strongest transfer-of-knowledge cases in this batch (alongside B7SP41/legumain): confirmed homodimer (direct UniProt evidence), correct insect-specific GST class identified by CDD, and MULTIPLE high-resolution ligand-bound structures from the same protein class in related arthropods (mosquito, housefly, fruit fly) directly implicated in xenosbiotic/insecticide resistance -- precisely the biology TickDock is trying to exploit (GSTs are a classical acaricide-resistance mechanism). Family and structural-transfer confidence are both HIGH. LOW human BLAST identity (32%) makes this an attractive selectivity profile too.

Q4PMC9.family: PNO1 family (tandem KH-domain RNA-binding protein), ribosome small-subunit biogenesis factor
Q4PMC9.family_evidence: UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the PNO1 family'; UniProt name: 'RNA-binding protein pno1'; Pfam PF17903 (KH_KRR1_1st) + PF22891 (KH_PNO1_2nd); InterPro IPR055211, IPR055212, IPR041174, IPR036612
Q4PMC9.oligomeric_state: UNKNOWN as an independent oligomer; functions within a large multi-protein complex (pre-40S ribosome / small-subunit processome), specifically in a defined complex with the Nob1 endonuclease
Q4PMC9.oligomeric_evidence: Documented biology: 'Interdependent action of KH domain proteins Krr1 and Dim2 [Pno1 ortholog] drive the 40S platform assembly' -- PNO1/Dim2 is part of a much larger ribosome-biogenesis machine (90S/pre-40S pre-ribosome) and forms a specific complex with the Nob1 endonuclease (domain-mapped by biophysics for human Nob1/Pno1), modeled onto pre-40S cryo-EM density (PDB 5JPQ) as part of the UTP-B oligomerization platform -- not a simple homo-oligomer, but an obligate heteromeric assembly-factor complex.
Q4PMC9.binding_site_location: Tandem KH (K-homology) domains bind single-stranded RNA in a sequence-specific groove -- INTRA-subunit binding surface (each KH domain independently contacts RNA) -- but the protein's biological role requires assembly into the much larger pre-ribosomal particle (inter-molecular, protein-RNA and protein-protein). PDB 3AEV (P. horikoshii KH domains, RNA-bound) was used as a homology template to model the human Nob1-Pno1 KH-domain arrangement: 'Nob1 sits on a C-shaped string of two Pno1 KH domains.'
Q4PMC9.site_residues_known: Not confirmed at residue level for this tick ortholog; KH-domain RNA-binding grooves are structurally conserved but sequence-variable, and no small-molecule-relevant motif was identified.
Q4PMC9.characterized_relatives: P. horikoshii KH domains, RNA-bound -- PDB 3AEV (used as a homology template, not a direct PNO1 structure). Pre-40S/90S pre-ribosome cryo-EM structures showing PNO1/Dim2 in situ -- PDB 5JPQ (ct90S pre-ribosome). No dedicated small-molecule-bound PNO1 structure was found.
Q4PMC9.chembl_target: Not identified -- KH-domain RNA-binding ribosome-biogenesis factors are not a precedented small-molecule ChEMBL target class.
Q4PMC9.druggability_note: POOR small-molecule target by conventional active-site criteria: this is an RNA-binding scaffold/assembly-factor protein (not an enzyme). The project's own local data shows druggable_pockets=0 (fpocket found nothing). Its 'binding site' (KH-domain RNA groove) is a nucleic-acid interaction surface rather than a classical small-molecule cavity. Also carries very high dog BLAST identity (73.7%, human_risk=true) -- poor selectivity prospects even if a pocket existed. Recommend deprioritizing.

Q8T9S5.family: Adaptor complexes medium subunit family (mu-adaptin) -- AP-2 clathrin adaptor complex, mu2 subunit
Q8T9S5.family_evidence: UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the adaptor complexes medium subunit family'; UniProt name: 'Clathrin-adaptor protein'; Pfam PF00928 (Adap_comp_sub) + PF01217 (Clat_adaptor_s); InterPro IPR001392 (Clathrin_mu), IPR018240, IPR028565
Q8T9S5.oligomeric_evidence: The AP2 adaptor complex is explicitly documented as heterotetrameric: two large subunits (alpha, beta2, ~120 kDa each), one medium subunit (mu2, ~50 kDa -- this target's likely role), and one small subunit (sigma2, ~17 kDa). Multiple crystal structures of the intact AP2 core confirm this stoichiometry directly (PDB 2VGL, 2XA7).
Q8T9S5.binding_site_location: Two relevant sites: (1) the well-characterized cargo-binding 'tyrosine pocket' on mu2 recognizing YXXphi sorting motifs -- INTRA-subunit, entirely within the mu2 C-terminal domain, and the site captured in numerous peptide-bound crystal structures (below); (2) the intact AP2 complex requires a large-scale INTER-subunit conformational change (C-mu2 relocating to an orthogonal face of the alpha/beta2/sigma2 core) to expose the cargo-binding sites from an autoinhibited closed state -- so pocket ACCESSIBILITY is gated by an inter-subunit conformational switch, even though the pocket chemistry itself is intra-subunit.
Q8T9S5.site_residues_known: Yes, precisely -- the YXXphi tyrosine-motif binding pocket on mu2 is mapped in multiple peptide co-crystal structures: CTLA-4 peptide TTGVYVKMPPT (PDB 1H6E), a non-canonical VEDYEQGLSG peptide (PDB 2BP5), the P2X4 receptor YEQGL motif (same site), HPV16 E7 peptide (PDB 9UUL), FCHO2 WxxPhi motif (PDB 7OIT). One of the most extensively peptide-mapped protein-interaction pockets in this entire batch.
Q8T9S5.characterized_relatives: Human/rat AP2 mu2 (AP50) -- many LIGAND(peptide)-BOUND structures: PDB 1H6E, 2BP5, 7OIT, 9UUL (cargo-peptide complexes). Full AP2 core -- PDB 2VGL (with a PIP2 headgroup mimic, LIGAND-BOUND), 2XA7 (active/cargo-bound complex).
Q8T9S5.chembl_target: Not identified -- mu2/AP2 is not a conventional small-molecule ChEMBL target (known clathrin-endocytosis inhibitors such as Pitstop target the clathrin terminal domain, not AP2-mu2, and no curated ChEMBL entry for mu2 was found in this pass).
Q8T9S5.druggability_note: The cargo-binding tyrosine pocket on mu2 is an extremely well-mapped PROTEIN-PEPTIDE interaction site (many co-crystal structures define exactly which residues contact YXXphi motifs), making it a plausible candidate for peptidomimetic or fragment-based design even though it is not classically 'druggable' in the enzyme-active-site sense (mu2 is a cargo-recognition module, not an enzyme -- no catalytic chemistry here). CAUTION: very high human BLAST identity (87.2%, HIGH risk, already flagged) -- this pocket recognizes a near-universally conserved eukaryotic sorting motif, so cross-species selectivity is likely to be very difficult; the pocket itself is probably even MORE conserved than the average sequence identity suggests, since YXXphi-motif recognition is functionally essential and deeply conserved across eukaryotes.
